title: Install or operate Krisis
summary: Deploy, inspect, recover, or uninstall the user-owned krisis command, schema-4 migration-compatible state, exact Stop hook, and release-pinned krisis/observer Clockwork service while retiring Decisions schedules.
use_when: Krisis should be installed or updated for the current macOS user.
The observer binding, hook, baseline, logs, database, Annals configuration, release selector, or recovery state should be inspected.
A diagnosed terminal observation or one proven-unavailable unbound source requires guarded recovery.
do_not_use_when: Only an account should be searched or read; use Annals.
A foreign hooks file should be merged, live retained state deleted, or a release performed implicitly.
outcome: A validated current-user Krisis installation with one periodic observer, exact hook, preserved legacy Decisions state, explicit Annals decisions-library configuration, and retired digest/review schedules.
effects: Default preparation stages a content-addressed release and registers and verifies its Clockwork definition while retaining maintenance without selecting or activating public surfaces.

Explicit final cutover migrates the database to schema 4, publishes the krisis command and providers, installs the exact hook and target-bound observer ownership receipt, selects krisis/observer, and disables only proven-owned enabled legacy schedules.

Uninstall removes exact owned public Krisis surfaces and disables its observer while retaining the database, releases, logs, legacy history, and Clockwork history unless separately authorized for deletion.
authority: The deployer owns release selection, exact artifact ownership, database migration ordering, maintenance gating, schedule handoff, and rollback.
Codex owns hook discovery and trust, Clockwork owns definition and runtime history, Annals owns its dedicated library, and Krisis owns observation and delivery state.
success: Preparation reports the candidate release and definition digest, retains maintenance, and leaves release, hook, command, provider, and binding selectors unchanged.

Final cutover reports krisis 0.4.0-compatible identity, provider releases match, doctor proves schema 4 and exact Conversations, Nucleus, and Annals readiness, and selectors resolve inside one validated release.

The write-once baseline exists before hook and krisis/observer publication, old daily and observer schedules are disabled, and a deliberate post-baseline completed user turn appears in observer coverage.
Routine observer logs remain body-free and account delivery reaches only the configured dedicated Annals library.
failure_and_recovery: A provable failed update restores prior owned selectors, hook bytes, database and sidecars, and schedule selection; an unprovable rollback retains the private maintenance gate and transaction backup.
Foreign, symbolic, hard-linked, modified, or ambiguous releases, databases, selectors, hooks, paths, selected definitions, ownership receipts, or loaded labels are refused rather than replaced.
Missed hooks recover with observe reconcile; pending Annals delivery retries before classification; terminal observation retry and unavailable-source abandonment require explicit guarded commands.
privacy: State and logs remain in the existing private Decisions application-support and log directories for migration compatibility; logs contain no account bodies, transcript text, prompts, or credentials.
The observer runner uses a scrubbed environment containing only explicit local paths, source configuration, and the expected Annals library identity.
Retired Decisions history is preserved locally and is not sent to Annals.
steps: Read the installation manual and inspect candidate, current owned artifacts, dependency contracts, exact Annals config and expected library ID, hook trust, and Clockwork state.
Run the release-owned deployer without --final-cutover to prepare and verify the exact candidate while retaining maintenance.
After external Annals and semantic activation proof, rerun the same exact inputs with --final-cutover.
Verify doctor, observer status, baseline, provider and release selectors, krisis/observer history, disabled Decisions bindings, body-free logs, and maintenance-gate removal.
Review and trust the exact Stop hook, then perform a separately authorized synthetic post-baseline canary on the actual Codex surface.
For uninstall, disable only exact owned Krisis state and retain database, releases, logs, and legacy history.
checkpoints: The public executable and command are krisis; provider is krisis; active Clockwork key is krisis/observer; daily and review schedules are absent or disabled.
Persistent database and log paths stay under Library/Application Support/Decisions and Library/Logs/Decisions for migration compatibility.
The Annals executable and config are absolute, expected library ID is exact lowercase 32-hex, and doctor validates decision-feed watermark contract and library identity.
A private release-independent maintenance marker gates the runner during quiescence, migration, selector switching, hook replacement, and schedule handoff.
The prior database plus sidecars is backed up only after exact owned writers are stopped and quiescence is proven; migration is sequential through schema 4.
No release, deploy, canary, live account acceptance, trust change, or retained-state deletion occurs without separate authority.
adaptation: Use alternate home and launchctl values only for explicit current-user test boundaries.
Diagnose dependency readiness at its owning product and never add direct fallbacks.
Treat retained Decisions lifecycle reads as compatibility only, not proof of Krisis or Annals readiness.
stop_when: Candidate, provider, schema, Conversations, Nucleus, Annals, Clockwork, or hook boundary is incompatible or unavailable.
A selector, hook, service, config, or state path is foreign or cannot be safely recovered.
The expected Annals library ID cannot be proven or a requested action would delete retained state without separate authority.

interfaces.label: Prepare
interfaces.invocation: decisions/packaging/macos/deploy-user.sh --binary ABSOLUTE_KRISIS --clockwork ABSOLUTE_CLOCKWORK --annals ABSOLUTE_ANNALS --annals-config ABSOLUTE_CONFIG --annals-library-id LOWERCASE_32_HEX

interfaces.label: Final cutover
interfaces.invocation: decisions/packaging/macos/deploy-user.sh --binary ABSOLUTE_KRISIS --clockwork ABSOLUTE_CLOCKWORK --annals ABSOLUTE_ANNALS --annals-config ABSOLUTE_CONFIG --annals-library-id LOWERCASE_32_HEX --final-cutover

does_not_authorize: Releasing, deploying, trusting a hook, executing a canary, invoking live account acceptance, or deleting retained state without separate authorization.
Replacing a foreign hook, changing Annals library identity, resetting the observer baseline, or restoring retired digest/review schedules.

consumers.statement: The current macOS user or authorized operator may install, update, inspect, recover, or uninstall the user-owned Krisis release and observer.
This is not a cross-user deployment, general hook manager, Annals library creator, retained-state deletion, or release operation.

preconditions.statement: Deployment requires a green exact krisis binary and matching provider, compatible dependencies, explicit valid Annals configuration, and owned or absent selectors and service artifacts.
Before migration, exact product writers are maintenance-gated and quiesced and a private database-plus-sidecars backup exists.
Hook trust, real canary, live deployment, and retained-state deletion each require separate authority.

inputs.statement: Deploy consumes absolute Krisis, Clockwork, Annals, and Annals config paths, exact lowercase expected library ID, product-owned package/provider bytes, current-user home, and current owned installation state.
Foreign hook files, ambiguous selectors, direct SQLite edits, arbitrary library fallback, uppercase IDs, and unapproved state deletion are not accepted.

outputs.statement: Successful preparation installs and verifies one content-addressed release and definition while retaining maintenance and leaving active selectors unchanged.
Successful explicit final cutover selects one validated content-addressed release for krisis and both providers, migrates schema 4, installs the exact Stop hook, and enables only krisis/observer.
Uninstall removes exact public selectors and disables the owned observer while retaining migration-compatible state, releases, logs, and scheduler history.

data_semantics.statement: The observer baseline is a write-once user-authority cutover; the Stop hook is only a wake correlation, and pending Annals delivery remains incomplete capture.
Content release, provider release, schema, binding key and definition digest, expected Annals library ID, and decision-feed watermark are distinct identities.

identity_and_units.statement: Public binary/provider are krisis, active Clockwork key is krisis/observer, schema is 4, and retained filesystem roots keep the Decisions name solely for compatibility.
Observer interval is 60 seconds and hook timeout is three seconds; library ID is 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.
Installation publishes no usage or billing unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Preparation verifies exact versions, content, definition fields, and library routing without activation; final cutover additionally verifies schema, dependencies, owned selectors, baseline ordering, owned legacy binding retirement, and active observer selection.
No service availability, hook delivery, observation latency, release retention, log retention, or repair-time objective is promised.

access.statement: Supported operation is current-user local filesystem and shell access through exact product, Clockwork, Annals, and launchctl surfaces.
Foreign, symbolic, modified, ambiguous, or unowned artifacts are refused rather than followed, merged, or replaced.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Preparation validates and registers the candidate while retaining maintenance; explicit final cutover revalidates closed release trees, private database files, definitions, and the target-bound ownership receipt, disables only proven-owned enabled schedules, drains the hook, backs up quiescent SQLite state, migrates, stages selectors, proves doctor, activates the baseline once, publishes hook and command, verifies krisis/observer, commits, and clears the gate.
Provable failure restores prior state; unprovable rollback retains maintenance gating and backup and does not claim external scheduler success.
Uninstall retains database, baseline, receipt ledger, legacy history, releases, logs, and scheduler history pending separate destructive authority.

operational_limits.statement: Standard operation supports one current macOS user, one krisis/observer binding, one exact Stop hook, explicit schema migration to 4, and serial observation.
No hook merge, trust bypass, baseline reset, direct repair, parallel observer, daily digest schedule, review schedule, or arbitrary Annals library is supported.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Krisis 0.4.0 and SQLite schema 4 preserve legacy Decisions rows and read decoding; public command/provider and active schedule move to Krisis identity.
No release-retention count, downgrade window, future migration path, or deprecation deadline is promised.

reliances.statement: Doctor and source operation rely on Conversations normalized history.
Classification readiness relies on Nucleus exact bounded execution.
Doctor and delivery rely on the exact Annals decision-account exchange and configured dedicated library.
Observer definition registration, selection, supervision, and history rely on Clockwork.
Hook discovery and trust rely on Codex, for which no installed Chancery contract is declared.
